eligibility_reason: Section 3.2 defines a persistent 'experience memory' table (task, observation, action, Q value) that the agent writes to at run time via an RL update rule, and Section 3.3 shows the agent retrieving similar past records to condition its next action; the store persists across episodes and even across different task goals (p. 2, p. 4).

facets.justification: Section 3.2, p. 4: 'the experience memory is designed as a table storing the task information, observation, action, and the corresponding Q value estimation,' with Figure 3 depicting the record schema (task/obs., action, Q value).

Section 3.2, p. 5, Eq. 2-3: a record is inserted only if (g, ot, at) is not yet present; if it already exists, its stored Q value is updated in place via the Q-learning rule Q(g,ot,at) ← (1-α)Q(g,ot,at) + αQ'(g,ot,at) — this update rule is RLEM's central mechanism (title, p. 1) and what Section 4's ablations (p. 10) probe.
Section 3.3, p. 5: a similarity function scores (g, ot) against stored (gi, oi) pairs and 'the m records with the highest similarities are retrieved to form the exemplars in the prompt.'

Evaluated on two public RL task sets, WebShop and WikiHow, against fixed-exemplar and prior-SOTA baselines with success-rate comparisons and ablations (p. 1, p. 2); no deployment, real users, or fielded setting is reported anywhere in the given pages, including the Limitations section (p. 10).

Abstract and p. 2: 'Extensive experiments are conducted on two RL task sets... average results... exceed the prior SOTA by 4% and 2%'; p. 10 reports further ablation tables (Table 8) on the same fixed task suites.

Contribution list, p. 2: '1) A new agent framework is proposed as REMEMBERER for LLM to learn from the experiences of past episodes... 2) We introduce RLEM, which updates experience memory...' — the paper's own framing centers on REMEMBERER as an agent architecture (LLM + experience memory + RL update pipeline, Figure 2, p. 4), with RLEM as the mechanism inside it.
